transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because I just… I feel like I can’t settle inside myself anymore. It’s like I’m sitting there, and even if I’m worn out and I know I should just stay still for a minute, something in me is pushing me to get up and do the next thing. I don’t mean just being busy, exactly. It feels like I’m uncomfortable in my own skin, like there’s this restlessness inside that won’t let me rest.

And I’m 66, so I keep thinking I should be able to just sit down and relax, but I can’t seem to. I’ll be tired, really tired, and still feel like I have to jump up or move on to something else. It’s gotten to where it bothers me enough that I thought, “I need to talk to somebody about this,” because it doesn’t feel normal for me to feel this unsettled all the time.
Did this restless feeling start after you began taking a new medication or after a dose was changed?

I’m not really sure. I can’t point to a clear medication change and say, “Yes, that’s when it started.” I mean, I’ve tried to think about that because it would make sense if there were some obvious cause like that, but I haven’t noticed a direct connection like starting something new or changing a dose and then suddenly feeling this way.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer, though. I’d probably need to look back carefully to be certain, because sometimes I don’t keep track of those things as neatly as I should. But from what I can tell, it doesn’t feel like it began right after a medication change.
When this feeling happens, do you feel a strong urge to keep moving?

Yes, definitely. That’s probably the best way to describe it. It’s not just that I feel a little fidgety or bored — it’s like there’s this pressure inside me that says, “Get up, do something, move on to the next thing.” Even when I’m exhausted, even when part of me knows I should just sit still and rest, I feel like I can’t really settle into that.

I’ll be sitting there and I can almost feel myself getting uncomfortable in my own skin, like I have to jump up. It’s not always that I have some important thing I need to do, either. Sometimes it’s just this urge to be moving or changing what I’m doing because sitting still feels almost impossible. It wears me out, honestly, because I’m tired but I can’t seem to let myself stop.
When you feel this restlessness, do you also feel anxious?

I’m not completely sure how to separate the two, honestly. Sometimes I think I feel anxious because the restlessness is so uncomfortable, like I’ll be sitting there thinking, “Why can’t I just calm down?” and then I get worked up about that. But I don’t always know if anxiety comes first or if the restless feeling comes first.

It’s not always like I’m worried about one specific thing, if that’s what you mean. A lot of the time it’s more just this keyed-up, unsettled feeling, and then I start feeling tense because I can’t make myself relax. So… yes, maybe there’s anxiety with it sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d say it’s always anxiety in the usual sense.
When you feel this way, do you find yourself pacing?

I do, yes, or at least I end up moving around a lot. Pacing is probably part of it. I’ll get up when I meant to stay seated, and then I’m going from one thing to another, almost like I’m trying to get away from the feeling inside me.

It’s hard to explain, but it feels like I can’t settle in my own skin anymore. Even if I’m worn out and I know I should just sit still, there’s this push to jump up and do the next thing. So yes, I do find myself pacing or wandering around, not always with a real purpose, just because sitting still feels unbearable.
Does moving around make the restless feeling ease up, even temporarily?

It does, but only for a little while. That’s part of what keeps me doing it, I think. When I get up and move, there’s this brief sense of relief, like I’m not trapped in my own body quite as much. But it doesn’t really solve it. It’s more like I’m chasing the restless feeling around.

I’ll stand up thinking, “Okay, I’ll just do this one thing,” and then I’m already on to the next thing, and then the next, even when I’m worn out and I know I should be sitting still. That’s honestly a big part of why I came in — I feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It’s like there’s this need to jump up and move on, and moving helps just enough for a moment that I keep doing it, but then the feeling comes right back.
Are you taking, or have you recently taken, any antipsychotic or anti-nausea medicines?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think so, but I’m not very good at remembering the names of everything unless I have the bottles in front of me. When you say antipsychotic or anti-nausea medicine, I’m trying to think if anything I’ve taken would fall into that category, and nothing obvious is coming to mind.

I haven’t, as far as I know, recently been put on something like that. But I’d probably want to double-check my medication list or the actual bottles, because sometimes I know what I take by “the little white pill” or what it’s for, not the proper name.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual?

I don’t think so… not in the sense of feeling like I only need a few hours and I’m perfectly fine. My sleep isn’t something I track very neatly, so it’s hard for me to answer with confidence, but I haven’t noticed suddenly needing much less than usual.

Sometimes I may be up and down or not settled, but I wouldn’t say I’m getting by on hardly any sleep and feeling rested or energized from it. If anything, I still feel like I need sleep. I’m just not sure I could give you an exact number of hours without thinking about it more.
Have you started taking an antidepressant in the past few months?

I’m not sure. I don’t want to say yes or no too confidently because I’m not always good at keeping the names and timing straight in my head. I don’t think I’ve started anything like that in the past few months, but I’d really have to look at the bottles or a medication list to be certain.

Sometimes I remember medicines more by why they were given to me or what they look like, not the actual category they’re in. So as far as I know, no, but I’d want to double-check.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about everyday things?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I do think about everyday things, of course—bills, appointments, whether I forgot something, what I’m supposed to be doing next—but I don’t know if I’d call it “a lot of worrying” or just normal life stuff.

Sometimes I notice I’m going over things in my head more than I probably need to, but I can’t say for sure that it’s constant worry. It’s more like… I get stuck trying to keep track of things, and then I might worry because I’m not sure if I missed something. But I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
When you feel this way, is it hard for you to stay seated?

Yes, very much so. It’s one of the main reasons I came in, honestly. I feel like I can’t settle inside my own skin anymore. Like even if I’m sitting in a chair and I know I should just stay there, there’s this push inside me to get up and do the next thing, or check something, or move around.

And it’s frustrating because I can be worn out — like really tired — but still feel like I can’t just sit still properly. It’s not always that I want to be doing something important, either. It’s just this uncomfortable feeling of needing to jump up, like my body won’t agree to being still even when the rest of me wants a break.
Does it feel like an inner urge to move in your body, more than a worried feeling in your mind?

Yes, that’s exactly how I’d describe it — more in my body than just in my thoughts. It’s like I can’t settle inside my own skin. I can be sitting there knowing there’s no real reason I have to get up, and even feeling worn out, but there’s still this strong pull to jump up and do the next thing.

It’s not always that I’m sitting there thinking, “Oh no, what if something bad happens?” It’s more like my body is saying, “Move, get up, do something,” even when I should be able to just sit still. That uncomfortable urge to move is a big part of why I came in.
When you try to sit still, do you find yourself rocking, shifting your weight, or moving your legs over and over?

Yes, I do. I’m almost always doing something with my body when I’m supposed to be sitting still. Like in church meetings, I’ll be sitting there trying to listen, and then I realize my foot is tapping and tapping, or I’m rubbing the edge of my purse with my fingers, or I keep shifting around in the chair trying to get comfortable.

It’s embarrassing, actually, because I don’t always notice it right away, but then I’ll see the ladies beside me kind of looking over, and then I feel like, “Oh, I must be doing it again.” I try to stop, but then before long I’m moving some other way. It’s like if I keep one part still, another part starts up.
Have you taken any medicine for nausea, such as metoclopramide or prochlorperazine?

I’m not really sure, doctor. Those names don’t sound familiar to me — meto… metoclopramide, or the other one you said. I’d have to look at a bottle or a list to know for certain, because I’m not always good at remembering medication names, especially the longer ones.

I don’t think I’ve taken anything like that regularly, at least not that I can recall. If it was something I got once a long time ago, I honestly might not remember.
Have you taken any medication in the past year that was prescribed for mood, sleep, nausea, or agitation?

I’m honestly not sure. I don’t think I’ve taken anything specifically for mood or agitation, at least nothing that I remember being prescribed that way. For sleep, I’d have to think — I don’t believe I’ve had a prescription sleep medicine in the past year, but I’m not always the best at remembering names or what every pill was “for,” if that makes sense.

Nausea medicine, same thing — I don’t recall being on something regularly for that. If it was a one-time prescription or something given briefly, I’d probably need to check my medication list or the pharmacy records to be certain. I don’t want to tell you no and then find out there was something with a name I didn’t recognize.
Did this restless feeling begin soon after you started any new prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

I’m not sure that I can connect it to starting a medicine, no. I haven’t really noticed it beginning right after a new prescription or anything over-the-counter. It feels more like something I just… do, and then later I realize I’m doing it.

But I may not be the best person to remember the exact timing unless I had my medication list in front of me. If I started something and didn’t think much of it at the time, I might not have tied the two together. So I wouldn’t want to swear to it, but I haven’t noticed a clear link like, “I started this pill and then the restlessness began.”
Have you been feeling unusually high, upbeat, or euphoric lately?

Unusually high or euphoric? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have moments where I’m in a decent mood or I get chatty if something catches my interest, but I wouldn’t describe it as feeling “high” or overly upbeat in a strange way.

I haven’t noticed myself feeling unusually happy or on top of the world or anything like that. If anything, I’d probably need you to explain exactly what you mean by euphoric, because I’m not sure I’d use that word for myself. But no, nothing lately that stands out to me that way.
Have you been worrying excessively about a number of different everyday things?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I worry about everyday things like anyone does, I guess — appointments, bills, whether I forgot something, things around the house — but I don’t know if I’d call it “excessive” exactly.

Sometimes it’s hard for me to tell what’s normal worry versus just my mind jumping around from one thing to the next. I can get caught up thinking about little things, but I’m not sure it’s the kind of constant worrying you mean. Could you explain what you mean by “excessively”? Like, do you mean all day, or not being able to stop it?
Do you find yourself worrying more days than not?

I’m not sure I can say “more days than not” with confidence. Some weeks, I do feel like I’m thinking about things a lot — little everyday things, like what I need to do or what I might be forgetting — but I don’t really keep track of it day by day.

It’s hard because if you asked me at the end of the week, I might remember the times I was worried and forget the times I wasn’t. So I don’t want to say yes if that means almost every day, because I’m not sure that’s true. I do worry sometimes, but whether it’s more days than not… I honestly don’t know.
Could you bring in or read me the names of all the medicines you are taking?

I don’t have the names with me right this second, I’m sorry. I know I should probably keep a list in my purse or on my phone, but I don’t think I have one that’s up to date.

I could bring the bottles in, though, if that’s okay — that might be easier than me trying to remember and getting something wrong. Or I can read them to you later from the labels when I’m at home. I just don’t want to guess and tell you the wrong medicine or the wrong dose.
